Demo guide

Joining

Enter a first name or callsign, create a four-digit PIN and enter it again. Both PIN entries must match. Use the same name and PIN to return. There is no game code.

This is a local demo. Names and PIN checks only work on this browser. A shared database is not connected yet. Use a practice PIN. PINs are hashed and excluded from the public board.

Show staff

  1. Choose “Show staff the demo” for the guided tour.
  2. Enter a name and PIN, then continue through the steps.
  3. Hold to reveal a role. Show the mission, private instruction and voting.
  4. Open “Player board” in another tab of this browser.
  5. Continue the tour to publish an elimination. Watch the reveal, then the red X on the board.
  6. Continue to the eliminated-player view and final results.

Run a rehearsal

Open Host controls. Close joining and release roles when ready. Use Next or the Timetable to move through phases. In Voting, open and close each group’s ballot and publish the result. In Eliminations, choose a target, confirm the private outcome and publish it when ready. Only published eliminations cross out names.

Use the Players page to adjust mission points, recover a connection or correct a player’s status. Corrections need a reason and stay in the event log. Resetting the demo clears registrations and progress on this browser.

The player board

All players remain on the board, grouped by team. A published elimination plays a six-second reveal and leaves a red X over the name. Pending victims, PINs, private messages and unrevealed roles are never included in the public snapshot. Reduced motion is respected. No flashing or autoplay sound.

Launch locally

From the extracted source folder, run python serve.py, then open http://127.0.0.1:4173. Keep the terminal open. No package installation is needed.

Next: the database

Connected Test Mode is disabled until configured and tested. Replace the local identity adapter with server-side registration and PIN verification. Resolve a unique player record from the selected event’s roster, use a stable database ID, rate-limit attempts and provide organiser recovery. A four-digit PIN must not be the only protection for organiser accounts or private event data.

The server must enforce roles, group access, votes and outcomes. The projector needs its own public endpoint. Test at least two real devices, then rehearse the expected 50-player load. The README contains the full backend plan.
